The commitment chain, calculated

Availability promised to the customer
  1. SLA99.9%The contractual commitment to the customer, with credits and penalties.
  2. SLO99.95%The stricter internal objective that keeps a margin before any penalty.
  3. Error budget22 min/ monthDowntime allowed per month at the SLO level. That is 4 h 23 per year.
  4. OLA per team99.983%What each of 3 teams in series must deliver for the SLO to hold.
  5. SLI≥ 99.95%The measurement of record: successful requests / total requests, over a rolling 30 days.
  6. Measured capacity> 99.95%What the platform delivers today, measured before committing.

Illustrative assumptions: SLO = SLA with a 50% margin on the error budget; 3 teams in series; 30-day month.

Measure before committing

An SLA is only enforceable when it rests on achievable OLAs, themselves backed by reliable measurements. I work at every stage of the engagement, from scoping to governance.

  1. Scope

    Assessment of the current state, service and dependency mapping, market SLA benchmark (cloud providers, banking sector).

  2. Design

    SLI → SLO → OLA → SLA model, service catalogue, commitment tiers, SLA/OLA traceability matrices.

  3. Formalise

    SLA and OLA sheets, RACI matrices per domain, documented and auditable calculation methods.

  4. Instrument

    Measurement built on existing tools, operational and executive dashboards, automated reporting.

  5. Govern

    Service reviews, ITIL processes, ISO 22301 compliance, roadmap and SRE adoption across teams.

About
